ace-of-swords.name: Ace of Swords
ace-of-swords.imageAlt: Ace of Swords: a hand emerges from a cloud gripping an upright sword whose tip passes through a crown hung with olive and palm branches, above bare mountains.
ace-of-swords.summary: The Ace of Swords represents clarity, truth and a breakthrough in thinking. Upright, it signals a sharp new idea, an honest conversation or a decision made with a clear mind. Reversed, it points to confusion, misinformation, harsh words or an idea that lacks the focus to succeed.
ace-of-swords.upright: Upright, the Ace of Swords cuts through fog. You see a situation clearly, perhaps for the first time, and can act on the truth. It favors honest communication, fresh ideas, study and firm decisions. Use this clarity with care, since words can wound as well as heal.
ace-of-swords.reversed: Reversed, the Ace of Swords suggests a blurred blade. Facts may be missing or twisted, thinking may be muddled, or words may be used to hurt. Gather information and wait for clarity before acting.

upright.short: A moment of clarity or a hard truth in the past changed how you saw things for good.

reversed.short: In the past confusion or a misunderstanding led you in the wrong direction.

upright.short: You see the situation clearly. Speak honestly and make the decision you have been weighing.

reversed.short: Your thinking is clouded. Check the facts and avoid sharp words until things are clearer.

upright.short: A breakthrough is coming: new information, an idea or a truth that clears the way.

reversed.short: Expect some confusion ahead. Get things in writing and ask questions before deciding.

two-of-swords.name: Two of Swords
two-of-swords.imageAlt: Two of Swords: a blindfolded woman in a white robe sits on a stone bench with two long swords crossed over her chest, a calm sea and crescent moon behind her.
two-of-swords.summary: The Two of Swords represents indecision, stalemate and avoiding a difficult choice. Upright, it signals being stuck between two options and blocking out information that would help. Reversed, it points to information overload, a decision finally made, or emotions breaking through a forced calm.
two-of-swords.upright: Upright, the Two of Swords shows someone holding two blades in perfect, tense balance with her eyes covered. You may be avoiding a choice because both options seem hard, or refusing to look at the facts. The card asks you to remove the blindfold.
two-of-swords.reversed: Reversed, the Two of Swords suggests the stalemate is breaking. You may finally choose, or feel overwhelmed by too much input. Emotions you have suppressed may surface. Either way, staying frozen is no longer possible.

upright.short: A difficult choice in the past, held for a long time, shaped where you are now.

reversed.short: In the past you finally made a hard decision you had avoided, and you live with its results.

upright.short: You are avoiding a decision. Look honestly at both options and choose.

reversed.short: The pressure to decide has broken through. Trust your judgment, even without perfect information.

upright.short: A choice between two paths is coming. Prepare by gathering the facts now.

reversed.short: A long stalemate will end. Be ready for the feelings that come with the decision.

three-of-swords.name: Three of Swords
three-of-swords.imageAlt: Three of Swords: a red heart pierced by three swords hangs against a gray sky filled with rain clouds.
three-of-swords.summary: The Three of Swords represents heartbreak, grief and painful truth. Upright, it signals emotional hurt, separation or sorrow that must be felt to heal. Reversed, it points to recovery, forgiveness and releasing pain, or to grief that is being held in rather than expressed.
three-of-swords.upright: Upright, the Three of Swords is one of the most direct images in tarot: a heart pierced in the rain. It describes hurt from loss, betrayal or a painful truth. The card does not soften the pain, but it suggests that facing it honestly is the start of healing.
three-of-swords.reversed: Reversed, the Three of Swords suggests the storm is passing. You are beginning to heal, forgive and release what hurt you. It can also warn against swallowing grief instead of letting it move through you.

upright.short: A past heartbreak or loss left a mark, and it also taught you about your own strength.

reversed.short: You have worked through a past hurt, and that healing has made you more resilient.

upright.short: You are hurting. Allow yourself to grieve and seek comfort from people you trust.

reversed.short: Healing has begun. Keep releasing the pain rather than holding on to it.

upright.short: A painful truth or disappointment may come. Facing it directly will help you recover.

reversed.short: Relief from an old sorrow is ahead. Forgiveness will bring lightness.

four-of-swords.name: Four of Swords
four-of-swords.imageAlt: Four of Swords: the effigy of a knight lies with hands joined in prayer on a stone tomb in a church, three swords hanging on the wall above and one carved along the tomb, a stained-glass window behind.
four-of-swords.summary: The Four of Swords represents rest, recovery and quiet contemplation. Upright, it signals a needed pause to recharge after stress, illness or conflict. Reversed, it points to restlessness, burnout, refusing to rest or slowly returning to activity after a period of withdrawal.
four-of-swords.upright: Upright, the Four of Swords calls for stillness. After a hard time, the mind and body need recovery. Take a break, step away from conflict and let your thoughts settle. This rest is not wasted time; it is preparation for what comes next.
four-of-swords.reversed: Reversed, the Four of Swords suggests rest is being ignored or is ending. You may be pushing on despite exhaustion, or feeling restless after a long pause. Listen to your body, and return to activity gradually.

upright.short: A period of rest or retreat in the past helped you recover and regain perspective.

reversed.short: In the past you pushed through exhaustion instead of resting, and you may still feel the cost.

upright.short: Take time out. Rest, reflect and let your mind recover before acting.

reversed.short: You are running on empty but refusing to stop. Schedule real rest now.

upright.short: A quiet period of recovery is coming. Use it well.

reversed.short: You may be tempted to skip rest ahead. Plan recovery before burnout forces it.

five-of-swords.name: Five of Swords
five-of-swords.imageAlt: Five of Swords: a smirking man gathers up swords while two dejected figures walk away toward the shore, two swords lying on the ground under a windswept sky.
five-of-swords.summary: The Five of Swords represents conflict, defeat and winning at a cost. Upright, it signals arguments, hostility and victories that damage relationships. Reversed, it points to reconciliation, letting go of a grudge, ending a conflict or lingering resentment after a painful dispute.
five-of-swords.upright: Upright, the Five of Swords shows a win that leaves everyone worse off. Arguments may have turned personal, or someone may be playing dirty to come out on top. The card asks whether being right is worth what it costs, and when to walk away.
five-of-swords.reversed: Reversed, the Five of Swords suggests the fight is ending. There may be a chance to make peace, apologize or let go of resentment. It can also show bitterness that lingers after the conflict itself has passed.

upright.short: A past conflict ended badly for someone, and the tension from it still lingers.

reversed.short: You moved past an old conflict, and that reconciliation still helps you.

upright.short: A conflict is costing more than it is worth. Choose your battles carefully.

reversed.short: It is time to make peace. Let go of the grudge and repair what you can.

upright.short: A clash of interests may come. Think about the long-term cost before trying to win.

reversed.short: A conflict will ease. An apology or compromise can close it for good.

six-of-swords.name: Six of Swords
six-of-swords.imageAlt: Six of Swords: a ferryman poles a small boat carrying a cloaked woman and a child across water toward a distant shore, six swords standing upright in the boat.
six-of-swords.summary: The Six of Swords represents transition, moving on and leaving difficulty behind. Upright, it signals calmer waters ahead, a journey or a gradual recovery after a hard period. Reversed, it points to resisting change, unfinished business or carrying old problems into a new situation.
six-of-swords.upright: Upright, the Six of Swords shows a crossing toward quieter waters. The swords still travel with the passengers, so the past is not forgotten, but the worst is behind you. It favors moving forward, accepting help and travel.
six-of-swords.reversed: Reversed, the Six of Swords suggests the boat is stuck or turning back. You may be reluctant to leave, or bringing old troubles with you. Resolve what you can before moving on, or the same problems may follow.

upright.short: You left a difficult situation behind in the past, and that move brought you to calmer ground.

reversed.short: In the past you could not move on, and some of that unfinished business remains.

upright.short: You are leaving a hard time behind. Keep moving toward calmer water and accept help.

reversed.short: You are resisting a necessary move. Deal with what holds you back, then go.

upright.short: A transition or journey ahead will bring relief and a fresh outlook.

reversed.short: Moving on may take longer than hoped. Clear old baggage first.

seven-of-swords.name: Seven of Swords
seven-of-swords.imageAlt: Seven of Swords: a man tiptoes away from a military camp carrying five swords and looking back over his shoulder, two swords left standing in the ground behind him.
seven-of-swords.summary: The Seven of Swords represents deception, strategy and getting away with something. Upright, it signals secrecy, cutting corners or someone acting behind the scenes. Reversed, it points to a deception being exposed, a guilty conscience, coming clean or a strategy that no longer works.
seven-of-swords.upright: Upright, the Seven of Swords warns that not everything is out in the open. Someone may be dishonest, or you may be tempted to bend the rules. It can also mean clever strategy and working alone. Ask whether your methods would survive being seen.
seven-of-swords.reversed: Reversed, the Seven of Swords suggests secrets are surfacing. A deception may be uncovered, or you may feel ready to admit something. Honesty, even when uncomfortable, will restore your peace of mind.

upright.short: A past deception, yours or someone else's, still affects trust in your situation.

reversed.short: Something hidden in the past came to light, and you have been dealing with the fallout.

upright.short: Be alert to dishonesty, and make sure your own conduct is above board.

reversed.short: It is time to come clean. Telling the truth will lift a weight.

upright.short: Watch for hidden agendas ahead. Protect your interests and verify what you are told.

reversed.short: A secret will surface. Prepare to handle it calmly and honestly.

eight-of-swords.name: Eight of Swords
eight-of-swords.imageAlt: Eight of Swords: a woman, blindfolded and loosely bound, stands in a muddy marsh surrounded by eight swords planted in the ground, a castle on the cliff behind her.
eight-of-swords.summary: The Eight of Swords represents feeling trapped, powerless and limited by your own thinking. Upright, it signals self-imposed restrictions, fear and a belief that there is no way out. Reversed, it points to release, new perspective, regaining control and realizing the restraints were looser than they seemed.
eight-of-swords.upright: Upright, the Eight of Swords shows someone who feels stuck, yet the swords do not fully enclose her and the bindings are loose. The trap is mostly in the mind: fear, worry or old beliefs. The card asks you to question the story you are telling yourself.
eight-of-swords.reversed: Reversed, the Eight of Swords suggests the blindfold is coming off. You are seeing options you missed and taking steps toward freedom. Anxiety may still visit, but you are no longer ruled by it.

upright.short: In the past you felt trapped by circumstances or your own fears, and that experience still shapes you.

reversed.short: You freed yourself from a limiting situation in the past, and that gives you confidence now.

upright.short: You feel stuck, but the limits are less solid than they seem. Look for one small way out.

reversed.short: You are breaking free. Keep questioning the fears that held you back.

upright.short: You may face a situation that feels restrictive. Remember you have more options than it appears.

reversed.short: Freedom and a clearer outlook are coming. Old limits will lose their hold.

nine-of-swords.name: Nine of Swords
nine-of-swords.imageAlt: Nine of Swords: a figure sits up in bed with their face in their hands, nine swords hanging horizontally on the black wall behind, the quilt patterned with roses and astrological signs.
nine-of-swords.summary: The Nine of Swords represents anxiety, worry and sleepless nights. Upright, it signals fear, guilt or overthinking that makes problems feel worse than they are. Reversed, it points to recovering from anxiety, seeking help and putting worries in perspective, or to despair reaching a peak.
nine-of-swords.upright: Upright, the Nine of Swords is the card of the 3 a.m. thought spiral. Worry, guilt or dread is keeping you awake, often more painful than the actual situation. The card asks you to talk about your fears and check them against reality.
nine-of-swords.reversed: Reversed, the Nine of Swords suggests the worst of the anxiety may be easing as you reach out or reframe your thoughts. In some cases it marks a peak of distress. Either way, support from others is important, and asking for it is a strength.

upright.short: A time of deep worry in the past still colors how you approach problems.

reversed.short: You came through a period of anxiety in the past, and that recovery gives you perspective.

upright.short: Your worries are heavy. Share them with someone you trust and look at the facts.

reversed.short: You are starting to see past your fears. Keep reaching out for support.

upright.short: Anxiety may rise ahead. Build calming habits and a support network now.

reversed.short: Relief from worry is coming. Things will look less frightening soon.

ten-of-swords.name: Ten of Swords
ten-of-swords.imageAlt: Ten of Swords: a man lies face down by the water with ten swords in his back beneath a black sky, while a band of golden dawn light rises over the distant hills.
ten-of-swords.summary: The Ten of Swords represents painful endings, rock bottom and the close of a difficult chapter. Upright, it signals betrayal, defeat or a situation that has completely run its course. Reversed, it points to recovery, surviving the worst, slowly rising again or refusing to let something end.
ten-of-swords.upright: Upright, the Ten of Swords looks dramatic, but its message is final, not fatal: something is over. The worst has happened, and there is nowhere lower to go. Notice the dawn on the horizon. Accept the ending so that recovery can start.
ten-of-swords.reversed: Reversed, the Ten of Swords suggests you are getting back up. Healing is slow but real, and the lessons are becoming clear. It can also warn against reopening a wound by holding on to what has already ended.

upright.short: A painful ending in the past hit hard, but it cleared the way for a new beginning.

reversed.short: You have recovered from a past low point, and that resilience is now part of you.

upright.short: A difficult chapter is closing. Let it end, and trust that things can only improve from here.

reversed.short: You are recovering. Keep moving forward and do not return to old wounds.

upright.short: A painful ending may be coming, followed by a real new start.

reversed.short: Recovery is ahead. What felt like defeat will become a turning point.

page-of-swords.name: Page of Swords
page-of-swords.imageAlt: Page of Swords: a young person stands on a windy hilltop holding a sword upright with both hands, looking alertly to one side, clouds and birds in the sky.
page-of-swords.summary: The Page of Swords represents curiosity, alertness and a hunger for ideas. Upright, it signals learning, asking questions, speaking up and new ways of thinking. Reversed, it points to gossip, hasty words, defensiveness or scattered thinking that never settles into real understanding.
page-of-swords.upright: Upright, the Page of Swords is eager to know. It encourages you to research, ask questions and share ideas, even if they are not fully formed. It can also bring news or a challenging conversation. Stay sharp and open-minded.
page-of-swords.reversed: Reversed, the Page of Swords suggests mental energy without discipline. You may talk more than you listen, spread rumors or argue just to win. Slow down, check your sources and think before you speak.

upright.short: A burst of curiosity in the past led you to learn something that still shapes your thinking.

reversed.short: In the past careless words or gossip caused trouble that still echoes.

upright.short: Ask questions and dig into the details. A curious, open mind will serve you well.

reversed.short: You are talking before thinking. Pause, listen and verify before you speak.

upright.short: New information or a chance to learn is coming. Be ready to engage.

reversed.short: Watch for gossip or hasty communication ahead. Keep your words considered.

knight-of-swords.name: Knight of Swords
knight-of-swords.imageAlt: Knight of Swords: an armored knight charges at full gallop on a white horse with sword raised, wind bending the trees and driving the clouds.
knight-of-swords.summary: The Knight of Swords represents ambition, drive and fast, focused action. Upright, it signals charging toward a goal, speaking your mind and cutting through obstacles. Reversed, it points to recklessness, aggression, impatience or rushing ahead without considering the consequences for others.
knight-of-swords.upright: Upright, the Knight of Swords rides into the wind at full speed. When you know what you want, this card supports bold, direct action and clear communication. Momentum is on your side. Just make sure you are heading in the right direction.
knight-of-swords.reversed: Reversed, the Knight of Swords suggests speed has become a problem. You may be bulldozing over others, starting arguments or racing toward a goal without a plan. Slow down enough to think and to listen.

upright.short: A burst of determined action in the past moved you forward quickly.

reversed.short: In the past rushing or harsh words caused damage you are still repairing.

upright.short: Act decisively. Pursue your goal directly and speak plainly.

reversed.short: You are moving too fast or too forcefully. Take a breath and consider others.

upright.short: A fast-moving situation is coming. You will need focus and quick thinking.

reversed.short: Avoid charging ahead without a plan. Haste could undo good work.

queen-of-swords.name: Queen of Swords
queen-of-swords.imageAlt: Queen of Swords: a queen sits on a throne carved with butterflies, holding an upright sword in her right hand and extending her left hand, clouds gathering below.
queen-of-swords.summary: The Queen of Swords represents clear thinking, honesty and independence. Upright, it signals sound judgment, direct communication and setting firm boundaries with fairness. Reversed, it points to coldness, harsh criticism, bitterness or letting emotions cloud judgment while appearing completely rational.
queen-of-swords.upright: Upright, the Queen of Swords sees through pretense. She has learned from experience and speaks the truth plainly, but without cruelty. The card encourages you to think independently, set boundaries and make decisions based on facts rather than pressure.
queen-of-swords.reversed: Reversed, the Queen of Swords suggests the blade has become too sharp or too dull. Words may be cutting, judgments harsh or old hurts may be shaping your view. Combine honesty with compassion.

upright.short: Honest, clear-headed choices in the past, yours or a mentor's, taught you to trust your judgment.

reversed.short: In the past harsh words or bitterness damaged a relationship, and it still matters.

upright.short: Be clear and direct. Set boundaries and decide based on the facts.

reversed.short: You may be too critical or guarded. Soften your delivery without losing your honesty.

upright.short: A situation ahead will call for clear thinking and honest communication.

reversed.short: Watch for coldness, yours or someone else's, getting in the way of understanding.

king-of-swords.name: King of Swords
king-of-swords.imageAlt: King of Swords: a king sits facing forward on a stone throne carved with butterflies, holding an upright sword slightly tilted, tall cypress trees and clouds behind him.
king-of-swords.summary: The King of Swords represents intellectual authority, fairness and clear-minded leadership. Upright, it signals logic, ethics and decisions based on principle and evidence. Reversed, it points to manipulation, abuse of power, rigid thinking or using intelligence to control others rather than serve them.
king-of-swords.upright: Upright, the King of Swords rules by reason. He weighs evidence, upholds principles and communicates with precision. The card favors professional advice, legal or technical matters and decisions made impartially. Let logic and integrity guide you.
king-of-swords.reversed: Reversed, the King of Swords suggests intellect without conscience. Someone may be using authority or clever arguments to dominate, or you may be so rigid that you ignore the human side. Fairness needs both reason and empathy.

upright.short: A fair, principled decision in the past set a standard you still follow.

reversed.short: In the past someone in authority misused their power, and it still affects your trust.

upright.short: Make a principled decision. Use logic, seek expert advice and act fairly.

reversed.short: Watch for manipulation or rigid thinking, including your own. Consider the people involved.

upright.short: You will need to take an objective, authoritative stance on an important matter.

reversed.short: Beware of someone using power or clever words for their own ends.
